items.name: Alex Ferguson
clues: Fierce, demanding and very loyal. Players who crossed him rarely stayed long.
Took a Scottish club to a European trophy in 1983, beating Real Madrid in the final, then moved to England.
Grew up in Govan, in Glasgow. While playing football part-time he worked in a shipyard and trained as a toolmaker.
Furious half-time talks: he once kicked a tea urn across the dressing room.
Retired in 2013 after more than 26 years at the same club, with 13 league titles.
Knighted in 1999, the year he won the first of his two Champions League titles with Manchester United.

items.name: Nelson Mandela
clues: Patient, dignified and forgiving. He believed you make peace with your enemies by working with them.
A country at the southern tip of Africa, from 1994 to 1999.
Trained as a lawyer and, in 1952, opened his country’s first Black-run law firm with his friend Oliver Tambo.
Spending 27 years in prison, 18 of them on Robben Island, then walking free in 1990 without seeking revenge.
Stepped down after a single term in 1999. He died in 2013, aged 95.
South Africa’s first Black president, known to many as ‘Madiba’.

items.name: Jürgen Klopp
clues: Loud, emotional and a big hugger. He builds teams that feel like a family.
Three football clubs in two countries, and at least seven years at each.
Spent most of his playing career at one German second-division club, then became its manager almost overnight in 2001.
Calling his style ‘heavy metal football’, and introducing himself to English journalists in 2015 as ‘the Normal One’.
Left his last club in 2024, saying he was running out of energy. In 2025 he went to work for Red Bull.
Won the Bundesliga twice with Borussia Dortmund, then the Champions League and the Premier League with Liverpool.

items.name: Steve Jobs
clues: Demanding, impatient and obsessed with detail. Colleagues said he could make the impossible seem possible.
A technology company that became one of the most valuable in the world.
Dropped out of college, then co-founded a computer company with a friend in 1976.
Wearing almost the same thing every day: a black polo-neck jumper, jeans and trainers.
Pushed out of his own company in 1985, he ran the animation studio Pixar, came back in 1997 and led the company until shortly before his death in 2011.
In 2007 he walked on stage and presented ‘an iPod, a phone and an internet communicator’ in one device: the first iPhone.

items.name: Jacinda Ardern
clues: Warm, open and calm on camera. She believed that kindness is a strength, not a weakness.
A country in the South Pacific, from 2017 to 2023.
Became her party’s leader less than two months before an election, and head of government at 37.
Having a baby while in office, then taking her daughter to the UN General Assembly in New York in 2018.
Resigned in 2023, saying she no longer had ‘enough in the tank’ to do the job properly.
The third woman to be prime minister of New Zealand.

items.name: Jeff Bezos
clues: Relentless, data-driven and obsessed with the customer. He liked to say that every day should feel like the first day of a start-up.
A company that started with one product and now employs well over a million people.
In 1994 he left a well-paid job at a New York investment firm and started selling books online from a rented house near Seattle.
Banning slide presentations from top meetings: managers write a six-page memo, and everyone reads it in silence before they talk.
Stepped down as chief executive in July 2021, and two weeks later flew to the edge of space in a rocket from his own space company.
Founder of Amazon.
